children: Stacks Labs is researching a design that would let Bitcoin holders borrow stablecoins against their BTC without giving up custody of it.
The coins would stay timelocked under the holder's control and keep earning yield.
The concept builds on Stacks' protocol bonds, which are anchored on the Bitcoin base layer. Users who stake BTC through these bonds would be able to borrow stablecoins against that staked position.
The BTC would remain locked, not transferred to a lender or a custodian. Under the proposed design, BTC used as collateral would continue to earn returns while it sits locked.
Stacks has said the lending mechanism draws on the infrastructure behind Zest Protocol. Zest has carried out over 1,500 liquidations without incurring bad debt.

That record is relevant because liquidations are where lending protocols tend to break. When collateral prices fall fast, a lender needs to close out risky positions before a loan is worth more than what backs it. Doing that more than 1,500 times with zero bad debt suggests the system has been tested under real conditions.
Bitcoin staking through protocol bonds launched on September 10, 2026. Self-custodial borrowing against staked BTC is planned for 2027.
As of mid-November 2026, three protocol bonds had drawn approximately 1,735-1,740 BTC, with major institutions among the participants.
Those bonds offer a targeted yield of 3% per year.

Stacks also has infrastructure goals tied to the lending rollout. The network aims for throughput improvements of up to 100 times current capacity. It also wants deeper stablecoin liquidity through its planned USDCx initiative.

The institutional interest in protocol bonds hints at who this is built for. If roughly 1,735-1,740 BTC has already been committed to a 3% target yield, a borrowing layer on top could make those positions more useful. Holders would earn yield and still be able to draw liquidity against the same coins.
There are real caveats. This is a research design with a 2027 target, not a live product.
The supporting infrastructure also has to arrive. The 100x throughput goal and USDCx liquidity are plans, and the lending market's usefulness depends heavily on both.

Liquidation mechanics also deserve close attention. Zest's record of over 1,500 liquidations with no bad debt is encouraging. But a self-custodial, timelocked structure raises its own design questions, particularly around how a protocol enforces repayment on collateral that stays in the user's hands.

The 2027 borrowing rollout will be the real test. Watch for progress on throughput upgrades, the arrival of USDCx liquidity and any published details on how liquidations would work for collateral that never leaves its owner's custody.

title: Stacks Labs is researching a way to borrow against Bitcoin without handing it over
